facts.statement: Higher cardiorespiratory fitness, which is separate from self-reported physical activity, was linked to lower white matter lesion volumes in the frontal and right parietal brain regions, along with higher volumes in the occipital regions.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The specific pattern of white matter lesion volumes linked to fitness was more common in younger participants and men.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The fitness-related brain pattern was associated with memory performance, specifically weakening the typical decline in memory with age, but it was not linked to information processing speed or executive functioning.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results suggest that higher fitness may help maintain cerebrovascular health in older adults by reducing white matter lesions in brain areas that are vulnerable to aging and memory issues.
facts.subject: humans
